newsitem.title: USA: Civil rights commission investigates Florida riot.
newsitem.headline: Civil rights commission investigates Florida riot.

text.p: The U.S. Commission on Civil Rights opened hearings on Tuesday night into race relations in St. Petersburg following the shooting death of a black motorist by a white police officer.

The Oct. 24 shooting set off rioting in the western Florida city. The rioting was followed a month later by more violence when a grand jury ruled that the shooting was justifiable homicide by the officer.

Leon Russell, chairman of Florida's National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People (NAACP), tried to focus the issue when he said, "what this whole thing is about here in St. Petersburg is the issue of justice, the perception of justice and whether or not the concept of justice extends to people who are part of the African-American community."

According to the police report of the incident, Officer James Knight stopped motorist Tyron Lewis for speeding on the night of Oct. 24. Knight got out of his car and was standing in front of the motorist's car because the side windows were tinted and he said he could not see through them.

Lewis began to bump Knight with his car, the report said. The officer warned Lewis to stop it, but Lewis persisted in bumping Knight with his car until he knocked him onto the hood. At that point Knight fired his gun, killing Lewis.

During a recent visit to St. Petersburg, Housing Secretary Henry Cisneros described race relations here as "a time warp" mired in the 1950s. The hearings are being held in an effort to bring better relations to the community, and Washington has pledged $20 million toward the effort.

Southern Christian Leadership Conference chairman Joseph Lowrey told the Commission "it is imperative that the economic imbalance in the community be addressed. Job training, housing, health care, education, entrepreneurship must be top priorities."
The hearing is to resume on Wednesday morning. Among those scheduled to testify are Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles, St. Petersburg Mayor David Fischer, and Police Chief Darrel Stephens.
